stories.headline: Nvidia beats with $115.8B quarter in first results without Huang, lifts FY2028 growth view to 75%

key_facts.fact: Nvidia reported Q3 fiscal 2027 revenue of $115.8 billion, up 103% year over year and 20% from the prior quarter; Data Center revenue was $107.6 billion, up 110%.
key_facts.excerpt: NVIDIA today reported revenue for the third quarter ended October 25, 2026, of $115.8 billion, up 20% from the previous quarter and up 103% from a year ago... Data Center revenue of $107.6 billion, up 110% from a year ago

key_facts.fact: Q4 revenue guidance is $130 billion plus or minus 3% (the quarter has an extra week), above the analyst average of just over $125 billion, with no Data Center compute revenue from China assumed.
key_facts.excerpt: The company expects fourth-quarter revenue of $126 billion to $134 billion, compared with analysts' average estimate of just over $125 billion, according to data compiled by LSEG. Nvidia said it did not assume any data center chip sales from China in its outlook.

key_facts.fact: Vera Rubin generated nearly $20 billion in its first quarter of production shipments, which Nvidia calls the fastest product ramp in its history; interim CEO Colette Kress raised the fiscal 2028 growth outlook to about 75% from 70%.
key_facts.excerpt: In its first quarter of production shipments, the Rubin platform generated nearly $20 billion in revenue, making it the fastest product ramp in NVIDIA's history... We expect revenue to grow approximately 75% year-over-year, up from 70%

key_facts.fact: Purchase commitments rose to $390 billion, and Nvidia announced new substrate and packaging supply agreements with Kinsus, Samsung Electro-Mechanics and SPIL.
key_facts.excerpt: Today, we are announcing new agreements with Kinsus and Samsung Electro-Mechanics in substrates, and SPIL in advanced packaging... In Q3, our purchase commitments increased to $390 billion

key_facts.fact: Kress said Hopper GPUs have recontracted at up to twice their original price under multiyear agreements and B300 rental rates have risen more than 60% since introduction; cloud industry backlog reached $2.5 trillion, up from $2 trillion three months earlier.
key_facts.excerpt: Hopper GPUs have recontracted at up to twice their original price under the multi-year agreements, while the B300 rates have risen more than 60% since their introduction... Cloud industry backlog now sits at $2.5 trillion, up from $2 trillion just three months ago

key_facts.fact: Board chair Harvey Jones opened the call saying the board unanimously accepted Jensen Huang's resignation and does not intend to reinstate him; Nvidia has retained Heidrick & Struggles for the CEO search.
key_facts.excerpt: The NVIDIA board unanimously accepted his resignation and does not intend to reinstate Jensen as CEO... we have since retained Heidrick & Struggles to lead the search.

key_facts.fact: Samsung Electronics rose 3.64% and SK hynix 6.47% in early Seoul trading Wednesday after the results.
key_facts.excerpt: As of 9:23 a.m., Samsung Electronics was trading at 199,200 won, up 3.64 percent from the previous close, while SK hynix jumped 6.47 percent to 1,169,000 won.

stories.headline: Nvidia stops shipping H200s to China; Tencent says new US remote-access rule will delay its next model

key_facts.fact: Interim CEO Colette Kress said Nvidia will no longer sell its H200 chips in China.
key_facts.excerpt: Nvidia will no longer sell its H200 chips in China, acting CEO Colette Kress said Tuesday, ending the company's participation …

key_facts.fact: Nvidia sold $2.4 billion of licensed Hopper data-center products to China in Q3; its guidance includes none, and it is no longer shipping them.
key_facts.excerpt: sales of licensed Hopper data center products to China was $2.4 billion. Our guidance does not have any licensed Hopper data center products included, and we are no longer shipping licensed Hopper data center products to China.

key_facts.fact: Tencent President Martin Lau said the new US curb on Chinese access to chips in overseas data centers 'sets everyone back in China' and will likely delay Tencent's next AI model.
key_facts.excerpt: "It sets everyone back in China," Tencent President Martin Lau told analysts on a post-earnings call on Wednesday. "It would take probably a longer time for us to come up with the next version in the short run."

key_facts.fact: Tencent strategy chief James Mitchell said cloud revenue will not be substantially hurt because it mainly runs inference, which efficient models can now do on a 'surprisingly limited number' of domestic chips.
key_facts.excerpt: Mitchell said Tencent's more efficient models could now be run on a "surprisingly limited number" of domestic chips. "We think that our cloud revenue will not be substantially adversely affected by the changes," he said.

key_facts.fact: Tencent said it may cancel some previously prepaid compute contracts it is exiting because of the rule, and that it can no longer offer high-end GPUs in its cloud outside China.
key_facts.excerpt: there may be some quarters where prepayments reverse due to the cancellation of contracts that we previously prepaid, but we're now exiting as a result of recent changes... When it comes to GPU, then unfortunately, we cannot actually offer high-end GPU anymore.

key_facts.fact: Under the rule, suppliers need a US license to ship covered chips and servers to overseas data centers that provide computing above a threshold to China-headquartered firms; Tencent and Alibaba were among companies using such facilities.
key_facts.excerpt: Under the new rule, suppliers must obtain a US license to ship covered chips and servers to overseas data centers providing computing power above a specified threshold to companies headquartered in China or other designated markets... Tencent and rival Alibaba were among the companies using such facilities.

stories.headline: SEC probes Nvidia as Huang offers to return and a board faction backs him

key_facts.fact: The SEC has opened a civil probe into Nvidia over whether its disclosures misled investors, the Wall Street Journal reported Tuesday; the SEC declined to comment.
key_facts.excerpt: The Securities and Exchange Commission is opening a civil probe into Nvidia over whether the company's disclosures misled investors, according to The Wall Street Journal.

key_facts.fact: In his first public statement since resigning, Jensen Huang said he would be 'honored' to return as CEO if the board decided it was in shareholders' and employees' interest.
key_facts.excerpt: Jensen Huang said on Tuesday he "would be honored" to return as Nvidia's CEO if the chipmaker's board decided the move was in the best interests of shareholders and employees

key_facts.fact: Despite the chair's statement, a faction of directors is pushing for Huang's return, and three directors oppose it, Semafor reported; Huang spoke with at least one director before earnings.
key_facts.excerpt: a faction of board members is pushing for his return... Huang has met with a number of tech executives and spoken with at least one board member about the possibility of his return... Despite the pushback from three directors

key_facts.fact: Arm CEO Rene Haas and Marvell CEO Matt Murphy have been considered to replace Huang; Haas has spoken to some directors but is concerned about the optics.
key_facts.excerpt: ARM CEO Rene Haas and Marvell CEO Matt Murphy have both been considered, the people said. Haas has spoken to at least some Nvidia directors about taking the job

key_facts.fact: Nvidia created a board committee on national security and export controls chaired by former Goldman Sachs vice chair Suzanne Nora Johnson; Huang still owns about 3.5% of the company, enough to nominate two directors.
key_facts.excerpt: Nvidia set up a board committee to oversee national security and export controls, chaired by director and former Goldman Sachs vice chair Suzanne Nora Johnson... he owns roughly 3.5% of the company, which is enough to allow him to nominate two directors

key_facts.fact: Further tensions may surface at an all-company Nvidia town hall on Wednesday; Jeff Bezos urged Nvidia to pick an internal successor.
key_facts.excerpt: Further tensions may emerge at an all-company town hall today. One former Big Tech CEO had a piece of advice: Amazon founder Jeff Bezos urged Nvidia to look internally for a replacement

stories.headline: Nvidia introduced Alibaba to Alice Huang in 2022, report says; House Democrats probe Lutnick ties

key_facts.fact: Nvidia's sales team introduced Alibaba to Alice Huang twice in 2022, helping her company land Alibaba as a customer and borrow money to buy Nvidia chips, The Information reported citing three people.
key_facts.excerpt: Nvidia's sales team introduced Alibaba to Alice Huang twice in 2022... The introductions helped Alice Huang win Alibaba as a customer, two of the three people told The Information... she got bank loans to pay for Nvidia chips

key_facts.fact: The aim was to give Alibaba access to Nvidia chips in Southeast Asia, a route US export controls did not cover until the Commerce Department's remote-access rule this week; Megaspeed was not the only company Nvidia introduced to Alibaba for this purpose.
key_facts.excerpt: The aim was to give Alibaba a way to reach Nvidia chips in Southeast Asia... Megaspeed was not the only company Nvidia introduced to Alibaba for this purpose, one of the people said.

key_facts.fact: House Democrats Jamie Raskin, Gregory Meeks and Sydney Kamlager-Dove asked Cantor Fitzgerald chairman Brandon Lutnick for records on whether Commerce Secretary Howard Lutnick blocked action on suspected Nvidia chip smuggling while his family's firm held Nvidia stock.
key_facts.excerpt: sent a letter to Cantor Fitzgerald Chairman Brandon Lutnick demanding records to determine whether his father, Commerce Secretary Howard Lutnick, blocked efforts to stop the suspected smuggling of advanced NVIDIA chips to China while his family's firm held hundreds of millions of dollars in NVIDIA stock.

key_facts.fact: The letter says Cantor held more than 3.5 million Nvidia shares worth over $1.3 billion at Lutnick's confirmation, cut the stake by about 49% while officials scrutinized the Megaspeed case, and sets a December 1, 2026 deadline for documents.
key_facts.excerpt: reportedly holding more than 3.5 million shares, valued at over $1.3 billion... Cantor Fitzgerald gradually reduced its holding of NVIDIA stock by roughly 49%... we ask that you produce the following documents no later than 5:00 p.m. on December 1, 2026

key_facts.fact: Cantor said its Nvidia holdings arise mainly from hedges on client equity swaps; Democrats cannot compel documents now but will gain subpoena power early next year.
key_facts.excerpt: "Cantor's Nvidia holdings arise primarily from equity swaps executed for clients..." While Democrats have no means or authority to compel the release of this information now, they are laying the groundwork for early next year, when Raskin and Meeks will have the ability to deploy subpoenas

stories.headline: GlobalFoundries becomes Boston Dynamics' first Atlas humanoid customer outside the auto industry

key_facts.fact: Chipmaker GlobalFoundries will be the first customer outside the automotive industry to test Boston Dynamics' Atlas humanoid, with testing starting in early 2027.
key_facts.excerpt: GlobalFoundries, a leading semiconductor manufacturer, will become the first customer outside of the automotive industry to test Boston Dynamics' Atlas humanoid. Atlas testing will begin in early 2027

key_facts.fact: It is the first publicly announced manufacturing customer outside Boston Dynamics' parent Hyundai Motor Group; the 2026 Atlas production run went to Hyundai and Google DeepMind.
key_facts.excerpt: The humanoids were earmarked for Hyundai and Google DeepMind... GlobalFoundries represents the first publicly announced manufacturing customer outside of Hyundai Motor Group.

key_facts.fact: The companies did not disclose how many Atlas robots, which fabs or which initial tasks are involved.
key_facts.excerpt: The companies did not disclose how many Atlas robots will be involved, which facilities will host the humanoids, or what initial tasks they will perform.

key_facts.fact: GlobalFoundries is also expanding use of the Spot quadruped; two Spot robots in Singapore have done more than 90,000 sub-fab inspections since April 2026 at a 99% mission success rate.
key_facts.excerpt: Since April 2026, two Spot robots at its Singapore facility have collectively traveled nearly 900 km (559 mi.) and completed more than 90,000 inspections in sub-fab areas, achieving a 99% mission success rate

stories.headline: SpaceX's $40B GPU financing heads to bond market this week, kept off its balance sheet

key_facts.fact: About $4 billion of bonds from SpaceX's $40 billion AI-chip debt package could go on sale within days, underwritten by Goldman Sachs and Apollo, Bloomberg reported.
key_facts.excerpt: Bloomberg reported that about US$4 billion in bonds could go on sale within days, citing some of the people... Goldman Sachs Group and Apollo Global Management are underwriting the expected deal

key_facts.fact: The financing goes into a special-purpose vehicle so SpaceX keeps the debt off its balance sheet and rents the GPUs; Apollo will lend close to $20 billion upfront and syndicate later, Semafor reported.
key_facts.excerpt: The financing will go into an SPV, or special-purpose vehicle, allowing SpaceX to keep it off its own balance sheet and instead rent GPUs from its subsidiary. Apollo will be lending close to $20 billion of the deal upfront

key_facts.fact: The bulk of the seven-part deal, $35.5 billion, will price at 8.3% and 7.75%; riskier tranches under $3 billion could exceed a 9% blended rate.
key_facts.excerpt: The arrangement includes an array of pricing — the bulk of which, $35.5 billion, will price at 8.3% and 7.75%... Other, riskier parts of the deal will price even higher, at a blended rate that could exceed 9%

key_facts.fact: SpaceX leases the chips for five years and cannot exit the lease if equipment fails or on force majeure.
key_facts.excerpt: Under the terms of the deal, SpaceX will lease the chips for five years. It cannot exit the lease if the equipment fails or if exceptional events known as "force majeure"

key_facts.fact: SpaceX called the Apollo-led lease, signed in October for Nvidia Vera Rubin chips, the largest committed GPU financing ever.
key_facts.excerpt: This lease will deliver the next generation of NVIDIA Vera Rubin chips for SpaceX's terrestrial compute buildout... It represents the largest committed GPU financing

stories.headline: Huawei's US racketeering trial goes to the jury Wednesday after two months of testimony

key_facts.fact: Closing arguments in the Brooklyn racketeering conspiracy trial of Huawei ended Tuesday; the government began its rebuttal late Tuesday and was to finish Wednesday morning, with deliberations likely to start later Wednesday (no exact hour given).
key_facts.excerpt: The government began its rebuttal argument late Tuesday and will finish Wednesday morning. The jury is likely to begin deliberating later Wednesday.

key_facts.fact: US District Judge Ann Donnelly was expected to charge the jury on Wednesday.
key_facts.excerpt: U.S. District Judge Ann Donnelly, a Barack Obama appointee, is expected to charge the jury on Wednesday before deliberations begin.

key_facts.fact: Huawei and three subsidiaries face 12 criminal counts, including racketeering conspiracy, trade-secret theft conspiracy, bank fraud and Iran sanctions (IEEPA) violations, in a case running nearly eight years.
key_facts.excerpt: The case has dragged on for nearly eight years, and the trial has been under way since September... Huawei and three affiliated companies face 12 criminal counts, including racketeering conspiracy

key_facts.fact: Prosecutors said Huawei helped Iran spy on its citizens and stole from US companies including T-Mobile and Cisco; defense lawyer Brian Heberlig said the government 'decided Huawei was a criminal enterprise' and worked backwards.
key_facts.excerpt: a prosecutor told jurors that the Chinese telecommunications giant helped Iran spy on its citizens and steal from U.S. companies and a defense lawyer accused the U.S. of embracing a false narrative... federal prosecutors "decided Huawei was a criminal enterprise"

key_facts.fact: Central to the bank-fraud counts is the 2021 deferred prosecution agreement in which CFO Meng Wanzhou admitted misleading HSBC about Huawei's Iran business.
key_facts.excerpt: At the heart of that charge is a 2021 deferred prosecution agreement signed by Huawei CFO Meng Wanzhou... admitting to misleading HSBC executives about the company's dealings in Iran.
